verdict.rationale: SigNoz documents service accounts for programmatic API access that are not tied to individual users. It also documents custom roles built from granular transactions that are granted to any principal assigned the role, which supports least-privilege scoping. However, the evidence never states explicitly that service-account credentials are scoped through these roles, nor does it describe agent-specific credential issuance. missing for 10: explicit documentation that service-account API keys are bound to custom least-privilege roles, details on key lifecycle (expiry, rotation, revocation), agent/MCP-specific credential scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Service accounts provide a secure way to grant programmatic API access to SigNoz without tying credentials to individual users.
any non-human system that needs to interact with the SigNoz API
A role groups transactions together — when a principal is assigned a role, they receive all the transactions that role contains.
managed roles, custom roles, and configuring transactions with the interactive or JSON editor
